text.p: Italy's Roma have made an offer for Brazil midfielder Denilson, club president Francesco Sensi was quoted as saying on Friday.
"Before Christmas I offered Sao Paulo $7 million and now I am prepared to raise the offer," he said in an interview with the Rome daily newspaper Il Messaggero.
It quoted Sensi as saying he had spoken to the young Brazilian's agent and a deal was not ruled out.
Sensi also appeared to distance himself from Roma's Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi, saying that with great players it did not matter much who coached the team.
"I am looking for players for Roma," he said, adding that the club needed three of four newcomers with two fresh midfielders at the top of the list.
Roma, who had Brazilian internationals Falcao and Cerezo in their teams in the 1980s, currently have Brazilian defender Aldair. Sensi made it clear that he would be staying.
The same could not be said for Bianchi.
"If we then have Bianchi or somebody else on the bench...I say that when you have great players in the squad, the coach could even be Father Christmas," Sensi said.
Asked why he had given Bianchi his backing only a few days ago, Sensi replied: "What else could I have told him?"
Other newspapers reported Sensi's remarks about Bianchi and interpreted them as a formal rift between the two.
"Roma: goodbye Bianchi," said the Gazzetta dello Sport, speculating that Bayern Munich coach Giovanni Trapattoni could be in line as the Argentine's replacement.

Bianchi joined Roma at the start of the season after a successful stint at Argentine club Velez Sarsfeld but the club has failed to gel under his leadership and looks in danger of missing out on European competitions next season.
Roma are eighth in the league, a point behind rivals Lazio, who have been linked repeatedly in the media with Barcelona striker Ronaldo, Brazil's other young sensation.
